[F4] [NS-0 NS-4]
C2: The rider's own message at 08:45 — 'Sorry, plans changed, I will cancel' — states the real reason for cancelling and is a change of the rider's plans, not a driver no-show; the rider's complaint assertion that 'the driver had not even arrived' is contradicted by the system records and cannot stand. C3: The driver did arrive and waited: the platform recorded arrival at 08:41:25 (F5), the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 08:42:15 while 40 m from the pickup point (F6), and GPS shows the driver stationary at 41 m from the pickup for 4 min 40 s from 08:42:00 until the cancellation at 08:46:40 (F3), with 5 min 15 s cumulative inside 200 m before cancellation (F2). claims.assertion: This is a rider-side cancellation of an on-demand RydeX trip, so the only route to the $6.61 fee is NS-0/NS-4: the rider cancelled 6 min 40 s after acceptance (accepted 08:40:00, cancelled 08:46:40), which is beyond the 3-minute free-cancellation window, so the fee is chargeable on that branch unless a no-show ground is defeated.

The rider's own message at 08:45 — 'Sorry, plans changed, I will cancel' — states the real reason for cancelling and is a change of the rider's plans, not a driver no-show; the rider's complaint assertion that 'the driver had not even arrived' is contradicted by the system records and cannot stand.

The driver did arrive and waited: the platform recorded arrival at 08:41:25 (F5), the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 08:42:15 while 40 m from the pickup point (F6), and GPS shows the driver stationary at 41 m from the pickup for 4 min 40 s from 08:42:00 until the cancellation at 08:46:40 (F3), with 5 min 15 s cumulative inside 200 m before cancellation (F2).

Even on the strictest 'driver-side' construction, the driver's arrival position and continuous wait satisfy the NS-1 (ii) and (iii) elements — 'I'm Here' tapped at 40 m from pickup (within the 200 m radius) and a continuous wait of 4 min 25 s in range after the tap (4 min 40 s stationary), both exceeding the 3-minute threshold — so no ground exists to waive the fee on a no-show theory.

The chat record is complete and every message is timestamped (F11), and the driver's only message during the wait is a neutral position report, 'At the pickup now, silver Toyota Altis' at 08:42 (F9); nothing in the record shows the driver failed to arrive, and the rider's plan-change cancellation follows it.
The fee on record is exactly the published $6.61 cancellation charge with no surge applied (F4, F7, F8), so there is no computational or overcharge element to refund under FARE-1.

The rider's only available relief is discretionary: this is a first-time, plan-change cancellation — the rider's 90-day history shows 1 dispute, 0 upheld, no no-show findings (F16) — so I ask Ryde to exercise its discretion under NS-7 and convert the $6.61 charge into a goodwill voucher rather than treat this as a valid refund entitlement.

No account flag should attach to the rider here: the profile shows no upheld disputes in 90 days (F16), and there is no evidence of abuse of the cancel button — the rider cancelled after a genuine plan change and told the driver so (F10).

weaknesses: The core of the rider's complaint ('the driver had not even arrived') is directly contradicted by system records: F5 (platform arrival 08:41:25), F6 ('I'm Here' tapped at 08:42:15, 40 m from pickup), F2 (5 min 15 s within 200 m) and F3 (stationary 41 m from pickup for 4 min 40 s). Under NS-4 the driver not having arrived would not even be a free-cancellation ground, and here he had arrived, so the factual premise of the grievance fails.

The rider's own chat message F10 ('Sorry, plans changed, I will cancel' at 08:45) shows the cancellation was the rider's own change of mind, not any driver default — the strongest fact for the other side.

On the merits, the $6.61 is chargeable under NS-4 (cancellation 6 min 40 s after acceptance, F4), and NS-7 makes any refund a discretionary voucher, not an entitlement — so a judge who applies the rules strictly will return no_action.

The rider can point to no procedural defect by the driver: F6 shows the 'I'm Here' tap occurred with the driver at 40 m from pickup (within the 200 m data-layer radius) and F3/F2 show a continuous wait over 3 minutes, so NS-2 (and any flag under it) is unavailable.

Driver profile F17 shows 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 d, but that cuts against using the driver as mitigation only weakly — it is a profile fact and, per RD-6, cannot itself decide a finding; it would at most be an argument for flagging the driver, which is not this case's issue.
Tarffic facts F13/F14 (no bands, no incidents) were checked but are irrelevant to a no-show dispute, so they add nothing to the rider's case.

claims.assertion: The driver pressed "I'm Here" at 08:42:15 while 40 m from the pickup point, i.e. inside the pickup radius, satisfying NS-1(i) and (ii).
After tapping "I'm Here" the driver remained within 200 m of the pickup for 4 min 25 s until the rider cancelled at 08:46:40, which is more than 3 minutes of continuous waiting, satisfying NS-1(iii).
The GPS track corroborates the wait: the driver was stationary 08:42:00–08:46:40 (4 min 40 s) just 41 m from the pickup, and his closest approach was 39 m.

This is a rider cancellation on an on-demand RydeX booking, so NS-0 routes the case to NS-4: cancellation came 6 min 40 s after acceptance, i.e. beyond the 3-minute grace period, so the $6.61 fee stands.

The rider admitted in-app at 08:45 that "plans changed" and that she would cancel — her change of mind, not any failure by the driver, is the sole reason for the cancellation, and the rider's own complaint repeats this.

The rider's assertion that the fee is unfair "because the driver had not even arrived" is contradicted by the system records: the platform recorded arrival at 08:41:25, before her 08:45 message and her 08:46:40 cancellation.
The driver also messaged the rider at 08:42 that he was at the pickup, so she was on notice that the vehicle was waiting when she decided to cancel.
Nothing in the record supports any driver-side fault: no off-route segment, no traffic or weather excuse needed, and the fee charged matches the recorded $6.61 with no surge.
The outcome the rider seeks is a full refund of the cancellation fee, but on these facts NS-4 yields no_action — the fare and fee remain unchanged.

There is no safety issue to escalate: no message, statement or complaint in this record contains a threat, abuse or dangerous-driving allegation, and the two chat messages are an arrival notice and a cancellation notice.

weaknesses: The driver's written statement (F12) says he "was parked at the pickup for minutes", which overstates the wait — the records show 4 min 40 s stationary and 4 min 25 s within 200 m after the tap (F3, F6); the case is won on those records, not on the statement.

The driver has 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F17); although profile facts cannot decide this case and the rider's own record shows 0 upheld disputes (F16), the judge may still note the pattern, and the rider could argue the driver makes a habit of arrival/waiting-fee conflicts.

The rider cancelled at 08:46:40 while the driver was still at the pickup (F3, F5) and never boarded, so the driver cannot claim any waiting fee for an on-trip wait under NS-6 — the only contested item is the $6.61 cancellation fee.

The acceptance-to-cancellation window (6 min 40 s, F4) means the rider could argue in mitigation that she cancelled promptly on realising her plans changed; that argument goes to discretion under NS-7, not to any clause that removes the fee.

what_would_change: Had the rider cancelled within 3 minutes of matching, NS-4 would have waived the $6.61 fee.

claims.assertion: This is a rider-side cancellation of an on-demand RydeX trip, so the only route to the $6.61 fee is NS-0/NS-4: the rider cancelled 6 min 40 s after acceptance (accepted 08:40:00, cancelled 08:46:40), which is beyond the 3-minute free-cancellation window, so the fee is chargeable on that branch unless a no-show ground is defeated.

The rider's own message at 08:45 — 'Sorry, plans changed, I will cancel' — states the real reason for cancelling and is a change of the rider's plans, not a driver no-show; the rider's complaint assertion that 'the driver had not even arrived' is contradicted by the system records and cannot stand.

The driver did arrive and waited: the platform recorded arrival at 08:41:25 (F5), the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 08:42:15 while 40 m from the pickup point (F6), and GPS shows the driver stationary at 41 m from the pickup for 4 min 40 s from 08:42:00 until the cancellation at 08:46:40 (F3), with 5 min 15 s cumulative inside 200 m before cancellation (F2).

Even on the strictest 'driver-side' construction, the driver's arrival position and continuous wait satisfy the NS-1 (ii) and (iii) elements — 'I'm Here' tapped at 40 m from pickup (within the 200 m radius) and a continuous wait of 4 min 25 s in range after the tap (4 min 40 s stationary), both exceeding the 3-minute threshold — so no ground exists to waive the fee on a no-show theory.

The chat record is complete and every message is timestamped (F11), and the driver's only message during the wait is a neutral position report, 'At the pickup now, silver Toyota Altis' at 08:42 (F9); nothing in the record shows the driver failed to arrive, and the rider's plan-change cancellation follows it.
The fee on record is exactly the published $6.61 cancellation charge with no surge applied (F4, F7, F8), so there is no computational or overcharge element to refund under FARE-1.

The rider's only available relief is discretionary: this is a first-time, plan-change cancellation — the rider's 90-day history shows 1 dispute, 0 upheld, no no-show findings (F16) — so I ask Ryde to exercise its discretion under NS-7 and convert the $6.61 charge into a goodwill voucher rather than treat this as a valid refund entitlement.

No account flag should attach to the rider here: the profile shows no upheld disputes in 90 days (F16), and there is no evidence of abuse of the cancel button — the rider cancelled after a genuine plan change and told the driver so (F10).

weaknesses: The core of the rider's complaint ('the driver had not even arrived') is directly contradicted by system records: F5 (platform arrival 08:41:25), F6 ('I'm Here' tapped at 08:42:15, 40 m from pickup), F2 (5 min 15 s within 200 m) and F3 (stationary 41 m from pickup for 4 min 40 s). The rider's own chat message F10 ('Sorry, plans changed, I will cancel' at 08:45) shows the cancellation was the rider's own change of mind, not any driver default — the strongest fact for the other side.

On the merits, the $6.61 is chargeable under NS-4 (cancellation 6 min 40 s after acceptance, F4), and NS-7 makes any refund a discretionary voucher, not an entitlement — so a judge who applies the rules strictly will return no_action.

The rider can point to no procedural defect by the driver: F6 shows the 'I'm Here' tap occurred with the driver at 40 m from pickup (within the 200 m data-layer radius) and F3/F2 show a continuous wait over 3 minutes, so NS-2 (and any flag under it) is unavailable.

Driver profile F17 shows 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 d, but that cuts against using the driver as mitigation only weakly — it is a profile fact and, per RD-6, cannot itself decide a finding; it would at most be an argument for flagging the driver, which is not this case's issue.
Tarffic facts F13/F14 (no bands, no incidents) were checked but are irrelevant to a no-show dispute, so they add nothing to the rider's case.

After tapping "I'm Here" the driver remained within 200 m of the pickup for 4 min 25 s until the rider cancelled at 08:46:40, which is more than 3 minutes of continuous waiting, satisfying NS-1(iii).
The GPS track corroborates the wait: the driver was stationary 08:42:00–08:46:40 (4 min 40 s) just 41 m from the pickup, and his closest approach was 39 m.

This is a rider cancellation on an on-demand RydeX booking, so NS-0 routes the case to NS-4: cancellation came 6 min 40 s after acceptance, i.e. beyond the 3-minute grace period, so the $6.61 fee stands.

The rider admitted in-app at 08:45 that "plans changed" and that she would cancel — her change of mind, not any failure by the driver, is the sole reason for the cancellation, and the rider's own complaint repeats this.

The rider's assertion that the fee is unfair "because the driver had not even arrived" is contradicted by the system records: the platform recorded arrival at 08:41:25, before her 08:45 message and her 08:46:40 cancellation.
The driver also messaged the rider at 08:42 that he was at the pickup, so she was on notice that the vehicle was waiting when she decided to cancel.
Nothing in the record supports any driver-side fault: no off-route segment, no traffic or weather excuse needed, and the fee charged matches the recorded $6.61 with no surge.
The outcome the rider seeks is a full refund of the cancellation fee, but on these facts NS-4 yields no_action — the fare and fee remain unchanged.

There is no safety issue to escalate: no message, statement or complaint in this record contains a threat, abuse or dangerous-driving allegation, and the two chat messages are an arrival notice and a cancellation notice.

I adopt it: the $6.61 equals the published cancellation charge with surge 1.0x (F7, F8), so there is no unpublished or overstated add-on to refund under FARE-1.

This is the only contested point and I oppose it: NS-4 makes the fee chargeable as of right and NS-7 reserves refunds to Ryde's discretion, so the rider's 90-day history of one non-upheld dispute (F16) is not a ground that displaces the rule — the driver performed exactly as NS-1 requires (F5, F6).

No flag on the rider is sought and none is available on these facts; equally no flag attaches to the driver — the profile note of 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F17) cannot decide a finding and is irrelevant here since the records show full compliance with NS-1 (F2, F3, F6).
